content:
presales-erin: Hey team — BankCo POC hitting early-token lag + spikes in TTFT. Baseline ~600ms, but after ~30s of steady 50–70 qps it jumps to 2.5–3s and we see some 429s referencing prefill queue. Dedicated trial (8xA100), model=redwood/growth-13b-8k. Can we swarm?

alex.chang: Can you paste an example request and the 429 body when it happens? Also are they enabling prefill/prefetch?

presales-erin: request headers (redacted):

```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"input":"<chat payload>", "max_tokens":512, "prefill":true}
```

429 response we got: `{"error":"prefill_queue_full","retry_after_ms":1200}`

bankco-sse: Confirmed. 429s show prefilling contention. We also captured some runtime logs around the spike: 

```
2026-03-18T15:43:12Z INFO request_id=abc123 qps=64 batch_window_ms=118 kv_cache_hit=0.18 prefill_locks_wait_ms=42
2026-03-18T15:43:13Z WARN request_id=def456 token_generation_latency_ms=2530 prefill_queue_wait_ms=1250
2026-03-18T15:43:14Z ERROR request_id=ghi789 prefill_lock_timeout true
```

maria.eng: Thanks — looks like two things: (1) KV cache hit rate collapses after sustained QPS which increases token gen tail, (2) prefill lock waiting causes requests to hit the prefill queue cap and surface 429. Batch window also growing to ~120ms which amplifies tail.

alex.chang: Quick experiments: ask them to toggle `prefill=false` or reduce `batch.max_delay_ms` to 20 and `batch.max_tokens` to 256. If TTFT improves, it's a prefill/batching interaction.

sam.ops: Pinging infra — are there any network egress blips or TLS renegotiations? bankco-sse mentioned TLS spikes in their sidecar metrics.

bankco-sse: We saw occasional TCP retransmits to kms endpoint around the same time but not consistently. Attaching metric query we ran: `sum(rate(tcp_retransmits_total[1m])) by (instance)`

presales-erin: Customer tried `prefill=false` and reported TTFT went from 3s -> ~900ms under same load, but cost increased because more tokens generated per-request without shared prefill. So they want a solution that preserves cost benefits but removes the tail.

maria.eng: Two mitigation paths: (A) tune prefill lock mechanism — increase lock shard count and bump lock timeout so one slow prefill doesn't block others, (B) adaptive prefill fallback: if kv_cache_hit < 0.3 then skip shared prefill for a short window.

alex.chang: Also add a short warmup phase (2–5s) that pre-populates KV for hot prefixes when traffic starts; that avoids cold-collapse after steady QPS ramps. We should expose this as a per-deployment flag so customers can opt in.

sam.ops: I'll check current autoscaler and GPU scheduler logs for queuing that could exacerbate batching. If GPUs are temporarily overloaded, batch_window increases.

maria.eng: I can prototype a small change: bump prefill lock shard to 16 -> reduces contention, and add heuristic to bypass lock if batch_window_ms > 80 and kv_hit < 0.4. Will run canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: job=56421 component=runtime-prefill-fix target=dedicated-canary-3
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: job=56421 status=running

bankco-sse: We're running the canary on a subset of their traffic now — will report TTFT and 429 counts in 20m.

presales-erin: Great — please post results. FYI customer is sensitive about pricing if we ask them to disable prefill permanently. Also sending them a short explainer for security reviewers re: locking change. :thumbsup:

maria.eng: Noted. If canary reduces TTFT tail and 429s without raising avg token usage, we'll push to prod and add runtime flag + docs.

alex.chang: For now recommendation to customer: (1) set `prefill=false` to stabilize latency during heavy burst testing, (2) reduce `batch.max_delay_ms` to 20ms, (3) we'll run canary for the lock/shard fix and follow up on cost impact.

presales-erin: Sending those steps + a short runbook to BankCo. Thanks all.

bankco-sse: Update after 22m: canary traffic TTFT p50=620ms p95=980ms, 429s dropped from ~12/min -> 1/min. Looks promising.

presales-erin: Amazing — I'll escalate to AE and pricing to discuss toggles and opt-in flags. Closing the swarm unless new regressions appear.
